evidence.quote: Fees should be separately stated, subject to court approval, with any reduction benefiting the class rather than reverting to Brightline.
Brightline would separately pay up to $6 million in court-approved fees and expenses; any amount not awarded would go to the class.
Class relief and attorneys’ fees were discussed during the same negotiations; fees were not deferred until after class relief was agreed.

summary: Plaintiff raised fees first, and fees were negotiated alongside class relief before the final class fund was agreed. The record shows no clear-sailing term, no fee reversion to the defendant, and no explicit tradeoff of lower class relief for higher fees. The court declaration accurately discloses that fees and class relief were discussed in the same negotiations.
